correctness.rationale: Pairwise exclusion of a distinct third joining edge gives exactly independence in the conflict graph, so splitting on selection of one vertex proves the frozen recurrence. A separately written enumeration rebuilt KG(5,2), C5 square K2 and their line graphs, used the exact third-edge predicate, and checked all subsets through size five. The vectors are (1,30,225,530,330,0) and (1,30,235,580,415,0); the zero at five rules out higher degrees by heredity. Independently acting by all 120 symbol permutations on every labelled Petersen-line-graph maximum reproduces sizes 30,60,120,120 and minimum-bitmask representatives {0,3,10,11}, {0,5,9,11}, {0,2,10,17}, {4,5,9,11} in the stated lexicographic indexing. A packing consists of vertex-disjoint induced stars: an extra induced edge or a third edge in a triangle or three-edge path would violate the test. In the line graph of a cubic graph every vertex neighbourhood is covered by two cliques, excluding induced stars of size at least three. The replay checks the reported component lists and the resulting counts 210 and 120.
residual_risks: The checks concern exactly the two specified line graphs and the specified S5 action, not an arbitrary cubic family or every symmetry of the prism.

value.rationale: These standard cubic graphs yield equal-order, equal-degree line graphs and the same maximum EOP size. Their exact packing distributions separate them even at size two and differ throughout the nontrivial sizes. The four symmetry types and component shapes classify every Petersen-line-graph extremizer, giving exact benchmark data not retrievable from the scalar maximum or a single coloring.
residual_risks: This is an exact result about a natural specified pair, not a general distinguishing theorem for regular line graphs or a classification of cubic packings.
